question: A container held 18 items initially. Through recycling, 14 items were removed (4 items). A delivery added 30 items (34 items). A redistribution removed 20 items (14 items). Another delivery added 17 items (31 items). A final checkout removed 7 items. Converting items to bundles of 4, this represented about 6 bundles. How many items remained?

A production facility started with 199 units. Operations multiplied by 7 (1393 units). Full-capacity operations multiplied by 4 (5572 units). Major maintenance removed 3722 units (1850 units). System failures cost another 1767 units (83 units). Emergency repairs added 60 units. Converting units to thousand-unit batches, this represented 0.143 batches. A competing facility had 200 units produced. How many units remained?

Two competitors tracked their scores. Starting with 235 points, the first competitor multiplied by 5 (1175 points). Bonus rounds multiplied by 6 (7050 points). Final challenge added 70 points (7120 points). Championship scoring multiplied by 3 (21360 points). Achievement bonus added 8 points. Derek scored 156 points in the same competition. What was the final score?

A warehouse manager tracked inventory morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 134 units, 79 were sold (55 units). Mid-afternoon restocking added 41 units (96 units). Late afternoon brought 25 more units (121 units). Afternoon sales removed 62 units (59 units). Evening closing removed 48 units. Converting to dozens, this represented about 0.92 dozen items. What was the final count?

A farmer tracked crop weight. Starting with 177 kilograms, 7 kilograms spoiled (170 kg). He received 39 kilograms in a harvest (209 kg). Weather loss removed 196 kilograms (13 kg). For 6 storage sections, he multiplied. Converting to metric tons, this represented 0.078 metric tons total. What was the storage weight per section?

Two business partners tracked quarterly growth. Starting with 50 dollars, they doubled (100 dollars). Investments added 80 dollars (180 dollars). Additional deposits added 6 dollars (186 dollars). Returns multiplied by 9 (1674 dollars). Scaling multiplied by 3 (5022 dollars). Final projection multiplied by 2 (10044 dollars). Converting to monthly amounts, this represented about 837 dollars monthly. Sarah's fund had 155 dollars. What was the annual projection?

Marcus and David compared earnings. Starting with 35 dollars, Marcus earned 25 more (60 dollars). Expenses reduced by 32 dollars (28 dollars). Side income added 6 dollars (34 dollars). Bonuses added 41 dollars (75 dollars). Annual projection multiplied by 9. David earned 48 dollars in the same period. What was the annual projection?

A project budget started with 217 dollars. Early spending removed 138 dollars (79 dollars). Grants added 16 dollars (95 dollars). Additional costs subtracted 64 dollars (31 dollars). Fee removals subtracted 11 dollars (20 dollars). For the full year, this was multiplied by 7. Converting to weekly budget, this represented about 20 dollars weekly. What was the annual budget?

Two traders tracked morning, afternoon, and evening transactions. Starting with 75 units, morning trading removed 8 (67 units). Mid-morning multiplied by 5 (335 units). Afternoon downturn removed 128 units (207 units). Evening losses cost 91 units (116 units). Final purchases added 16 units. Converting units to dozens, this represented about 11 dozen. Elena had 89 units of similar assets. How many units remained?

Two teams tracked performance morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 114 points, first half divided by 2 (57 points). Mid-morning bonuses added 80 points (137 points). Afternoon penalties removed 87 points (50 points). Evening adjustments removed 32 points (18 points). Championship multiplied by 6 (108 points). Final round multiplied by 9 (972 points). Marcus's team had 143 points. What was the final score?

A budget projection started with 217 dollars. Unexpected costs removed 199 dollars (18 dollars). Strategic expansion multiplied by 9 (162 dollars). Market opportunity multiplied by 5 (810 dollars). Final allocation added 34 dollars. Converting to weekly budgets, this represented about 116 weekly spending. A contingency fund had 95 dollars but wasn't included. What was the final allocation?

A computer storage started with 171 gigabytes. A large upload added 51 gigabytes (222 GB). The storage was then doubled for a backup (444 GB). A second backup doubled again (888 GB). Final consolidation added 17 gigabytes. Converting to terabytes, this represented about 0.9 TB. What was the total storage?

A fundraiser started with 50 dollars. Morning collections added 42 dollars (92 dollars). Early afternoon expenses removed 23 dollars (69 dollars). Afternoon donations added 68 dollars (137 dollars). Late afternoon brought 55 more dollars (192 dollars). Final expenses removed 143 dollars. A volunteer had contributed 85 dollars separately. How much remained in the fund?

A gardener tracked seedling growth. Starting with 111 seedlings, disease removed 80 (31 seedlings). A successful propagation added 42 (73 seedlings). Transplanting used 22 (51 seedlings). A new shipment added 67 seedlings. Converting to dozens, this represented about 9.9 dozen seedlings. How many seedlings remained?

A warehouse tracked inventory morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 197 units, morning restock added 28 (225 units). Major sales removed 189 units (36 units). Afternoon restocking multiplied by 9 (324 units). Evening consolidation divided by 3 (108 units). Final evening orders added 72 units. What was the evening inventory?

A bakery started with 205 loaves. Morning production multiplied by 8 (1640 loaves). Mid-morning hand-made additions added 4 (1644 loaves). Redistribution to 6 locations divided by 6 (274 loaves per location). Final preparation multiplied by 9 for quality checks. Converting to dozens, this represented about 206 dozen loaves. How many loaves per location after final preparation?

A factory tracked one production line. Starting with 160 units, equipment maintenance removed 98 (62 units). Afternoon shift multiplied by 5 (310 units). Quality control additions added 26 (336 units). Late afternoon brought 22 more units (358 units). Daily output was multiplied by 4 (1432 units). Final batch additions added 77 units. How many units total at day's end?

Two coaches tracked athlete counts. Starting with 114 athletes, registrations added 20 (134 athletes). Early drop-outs removed 16 (118 athletes). Mid-season injuries removed 65 (53 athletes). Final roster cuts removed 33 athletes. Marcus's team had 95 athletes in their program. What was the final roster size?

A production facility started with 63 work units. System downtime removed 53 units (10 units). The remaining work was divided equally by 2 shifts (5 units per shift). One shift was multiplied by 4 (20 units). Bonus overtime added 62 units (82 units). The total was multiplied by 3 (246 units). Final reduction removed 67 units. A neighboring facility had 140 units. What was the final output?

A company tracked productivity morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 78 work hours, morning brought 79 additional hours (157 hours). Mid-morning showed 27 more hours of work (184 hours). Afternoon multiplied by 3 (552 hours). Evening workload was halved by automation (276 hours). Late evening showed 96 hours of completed work left. How many work-hours remained?

A project tracked tasks morning, afternoon, and evening. Starting with 69 tasks, morning review removed 17 (52 tasks). Afternoon work multiplied by 7 (364 tasks). Late afternoon additions added 42 (406 tasks). For evening preparation, this was doubled (812 tasks). What was the evening task count?

A library started with 47 books checked out. Morning returns removed 16 (31 books). Mid-morning tripled acquisitions (93 books). Afternoon cataloging lost 62 due to inventory adjustments (31 books). Evening reshelving added 67 books back. Converting units to thousands, this represented 0.098 thousand books. A distraction: sister library had 75 books. How many books were in the collection?

David and Sarah managed a growing fund. Starting with 161 dollars, it tripled through investments (483 dollars). Grant additions added 61 dollars (544 dollars). Quarterly multiplier applied 6 times (3264 dollars). Annual expansion multiplied by 3 (9792 dollars). Final maturation halved (4896 dollars). Marcus had a separate fund of 200 dollars. What was the final matured amount?

Two team members tracked contributions. Starting with 188 hours, one added 24 hours (212 hours). A major project removed 99 hours (113 hours). Work multiplied by 5 for full-year planning (565 hours). Bonus work added 56 hours. Marcus contributed 78 separate hours to a different project. What was the final annual commitment?

David and Sarah managed a shared account. Starting with 226 dollars, initial withdrawal removed 31 (195 dollars). A deposit added 3 dollars (198 dollars). Investment contributions added 52 dollars (250 dollars). Growth multiplied by 9 (2250 dollars). Distribution divided by 5 equally among accounts. Twice the final amount would equal Sarah's entire savings. How much per distributed account?
